content.title: I. Antiplatelet drugs
content.Aspirin: Loading dose (LD) 150–300 mg orally or 75–250 mg i.v. if oral ingestion not possible, followed by maintenance dose (MD) 75–100 mg once daily; no specific dose adjustment in CKD patients.

P2Y12 receptor inhibitors (oral or i.v.).Clopidogrel: LD 300–600 mg orally, followed by MD 75 mg once daily. In fibrinolysis: an initial dose of 300 mg (75 mg for patients older than 75 years). No specific dose adjustment in CKD patients noted.
P2Y12 receptor inhibitors (oral or i.v.).Prasugrel: LD 60 mg orally, followed by MD 10 mg once daily. For body weight <60 kg, MD 5 mg once daily is recommended. In patients aged ≥75 years use with caution; MD 5 mg may be used if treatment is necessary. Prior stroke is a contraindication.
P2Y12 receptor inhibitors (oral or i.v.).Ticagrelor: LD 180 mg orally, followed by MD 90 mg twice daily; no specific dose adjustment in CKD patients.
P2Y12 receptor inhibitors (oral or i.v.).Cangrelor: Bolus 30 mcg/kg i.v. followed by infusion 4 mcg/kg/min for at least 2 hours or the duration of the procedure. When transitioning from cangrelor to a thienopyridine, give the thienopyridine immediately after discontinuation of cangrelor with an LD (eg, clopidogrel 600 mg or prasugrel 60 mg); prasugrel may also be given 30 min before stopping the cangrelor infusion. Ticagrelor (LD 180 mg) should be administered at the time of PCI to minimize gap in platelet inhibition.

GP IIb/IIIa receptor inhibitors (i.v.).Eptifibatide: Double bolus of 180 mcg/kg i.v. (given at a 10-min interval) followed by infusion of 2.0 mcg/kg/min for up to 18 hours. For reduced renal function (eg, CrCl 30–50 mL/min) dosing adjustments described (lower maintenance infusion). Second LD if PCI (180 mcg/kg) may be given per protocol. Contraindicated in end-stage renal disease and with prior intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), ischemic stroke within 30 days, recent fibrinolysis, or platelet count <100,000/mm3.

Associated Conditions: Target of P2Y12 receptor inhibitors (antiplatelet therapy)
Use in acute coronary syndromes and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)
genes.context: Page header 'P2Y12 receptor inhibitors (oral or i.v.)' and multiple drugs (clopidogrel, prasugrel, ticagrelor, cangrelor) are described as P2Y12 receptor inhibitors used in PCI and in the context of fibrinolysis.

Associated Conditions: Component of the platelet GP IIb/IIIa receptor complex (role in platelet aggregation)
Target of GP IIb/IIIa inhibitor therapy during PCI
genes.context: Page section 'GP IIb/IIIa receptor inhibitors (i.v.)' and eptifibatide dosing/contraindications refer to inhibition of the GP IIb/IIIa platelet receptor complex (glycoprotein IIb is encoded by ITGA2B).
